desc: S. 4784 is the current state of play and the thinnest point in the record. Introduced by Chairman Wicker and reported by the Senate Armed Services Committee in June 2026 as Calendar No. 436, Report No. 119-127, the FY2027 NDAA contains no unidentified anomalous phenomena provisions whatsoever. A full-text search of the reported bill returns zero occurrences of 'unidentified', zero of 'UAP', zero of 'Anomaly Resolution' and zero citations to 50 U.S.C. 3373. The eleven occurrences of 'anomalous' in the bill all concern Anomalous Health Incidents, an unrelated subject, or anomalous behaviour of software agents and autonomous weapons. Senator Rounds's own 16 June 2026 announcement of roughly forty provisions he secured in the committee markup contains no UAP item. This is the second consecutive authorisation cycle in which the subject has been excluded from the Senate's base text, which leaves only the floor-amendment route — and the FY2026 precedent is that there was no open amendment process at all, the bill being disposed of with seventeen amendments in total. Senator Rounds nonetheless stated in late June 2026 that he is 'once again cosponsoring' the UAP Disclosure Act as an amendment to this year's NDAA.
